# 1 Maccabees Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_016_page_001.jpg

---

**1** John came up from Gazara and briefed his father Simon on what Cendebaeus had been up to.

**2** Simon called in his two older sons, Judas and John, and said: "My brothers and I and our whole family have been fighting Israel's wars since we were young. God has used us to rescue Israel many times.

**3** But I am old now, and you — by God's grace — are in your prime. Step into my place and your uncle's place. Go and fight for our people. May Heaven be on your side."

**4** He raised an army from the countryside: twenty thousand infantry and cavalry. They marched against Cendebaeus and camped for the night at Modein.

**5** At dawn they moved out onto the plain. A large enemy force came to meet them — foot soldiers and cavalry — with a stream running between the two armies.

**6** John brought his men up to the streambank and prepared to fight. He could see that his men were hesitating about crossing. So he went first. When they saw him go, they followed.

**7** He split his force, putting the cavalry in between the infantry units, because the enemy's cavalry was massive.

**8** The trumpets sounded. Cendebaeus broke. His men went down in heaps; the survivors ran for the nearest stronghold.

**9** John's brother Judas was wounded in the fighting, but John kept pressing the pursuit all the way to Kidron — the very town Cendebaeus had built.

**10** The fleeing enemy scattered into the towers around Azotus. John burned them out. About two thousand men died. He came home to Judea in peace.

**11** A man named Ptolemy son of Abubus was the commander of the Jericho region. He had made himself very wealthy —

**12** and he had married into power: he was the high priest's son-in-law.

**13** Power and money inflated him. He began dreaming of seizing the whole country for himself. He laid a trap for Simon and his sons.

**14** Simon was on an inspection tour of the towns, checking on their welfare. He came down to Jericho in 134 BCE, in the month of Shebat, with his sons Mattathias and Judas.

**15** Ptolemy received them at a small fort he had built called Dok. He threw them a magnificent banquet — and hid armed men inside.

**16** When Simon and his sons had drunk themselves into a stupor, Ptolemy gave the signal. His hidden men grabbed their weapons and burst into the dining room. They cut down Simon, his two sons, and several servants.

**17** It was a vile act of treachery — he repaid every good Simon had done him with murder.

**18** Ptolemy immediately wrote to Antiochus, asking for military backup and requesting that the king formally hand over the country and its cities to him.

**19** He dispatched assassins to Gazara to kill John, and sent letters to the regional commanders inviting them to defect to him in exchange for silver, gold, and gifts.

**20** He also sent forces to capture Jerusalem and the temple mount.

**21** But a man ran ahead of them and got to John at Gazara first: "Your father is dead. Your brothers are dead. And there are men on their way right now to kill you."

**22** The news hit John like a blow. He pulled himself together fast. He seized the would-be assassins who had come to kill him and had them executed — he knew exactly what they had been sent to do.

**23** As for the rest of John's story — his wars, his military achievements, the walls he built, everything he accomplished —

**24** it is all written down in the record book of his high priesthood, from the day he succeeded his father.
